raw_text:
# 12-Week General Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 42-year-old male, sedentary desk worker, 8 months post L4-L5 disc herniation, currently asymptomatic. Physio restrictions: no heavy spinal loading, no loaded spinal flexion.

## Programming Principles

Given the history, this programme is built around three non-negotiables:

1. **No loaded spinal flexion** — that means no conventional deadlifts off the floor, no Jefferson curls, no good mornings with significant ROM, no loaded sit-ups or weighted Russian twists, no kettlebell swings until late in the programme.
2. **No heavy axial loading** — back squats with maximal loads, standing overhead presses with near-max weight, and heavy barbell rows are off the table. We'll use trap bar, front-loaded, machine, and unilateral variants to limit compressive spinal load.
3. **Build a robust trunk** — anti-extension, anti-rotation, and anti-lateral flexion work (McGill-style) takes the place of crunches and twists throughout.

Three sessions per week, full-body bias, with progressive intensity across three phases.

---

## Phase 1 — Reconditioning & Movement Quality (Weeks 1-4)

**Goal:** Re-pattern hinge, squat, push, pull. Build trunk endurance. Stay submaximal — all working sets should leave 3-4 reps in reserve (RIR).

### Session A (e.g. Monday)

- Goblet box squat to a high box — 3 × 8
- Single-arm dumbbell bench press — 3 × 10 each side
- Chest-supported dumbbell row — 3 × 10
- Half-kneeling cable anti-rotation press (Pallof) — 3 × 10 each side
- Side plank — 3 × 20-30 sec each side
- Dead bug, slow tempo — 3 × 8 each side

### Session B (e.g. Wednesday)

- Trap bar deadlift from blocks (mid-shin height, neutral spine emphasis) — 3 × 6
- Standing landmine press — 3 × 8 each side
- Lat pulldown, neutral grip — 3 × 10
- Front-foot-elevated split squat (bodyweight or light DBs) — 3 × 8 each side
- McGill curl-up — 3 × 8 holds of 5 sec
- Bird-dog — 3 × 6 each side

### Session C (e.g. Friday)

- Leg press (moderate depth, lower back stays flat against pad) — 3 × 10
- Seated cable row — 3 × 10
- Half-kneeling single-arm DB press — 3 × 8 each side
- DB Romanian deadlift, light, hinge to mid-shin only — 3 × 8
- Suitcase carry — 3 × 30m each side
- Side plank with reach-through (slow) — 2 × 8 each side

**Weekly progression:**
- Week 1: get baseline loads, focus on tempo (3-second eccentrics).
- Week 2: add one rep per set across the board.
- Week 3: add ~5% load on main lifts.
- Week 4: deload — drop sets by one and reduce load 10%.

---

## Phase 2 — Strength Development (Weeks 5-8)

**Goal:** Build genuine strength on safe patterns. Working sets at 2-3 RIR. Carries and trunk work get heavier.

### Session A

- Front squat OR safety bar squat — 4 × 5
- Flat barbell bench press — 4 × 6
- Single-arm DB row, chest supported — 4 × 8 each side
- Pallof press with rotation hold — 3 × 8 each side
- Hanging knee raise (controlled, no swing) — 3 × 8
- Side plank, feet stacked — 3 × 30-45 sec each side

### Session B

- Trap bar deadlift from low blocks (~mid-shin to just below knee) — 4 × 5
- Standing single-arm landmine press — 3 × 6 each side
- Weighted chin-up or assisted chin-up — 4 × 6
- Reverse lunge with front-rack DBs — 3 × 8 each side
- Farmer's carry — 3 × 40m, building load weekly
- Bird-dog with band — 3 × 6 each side

### Session C

- Bulgarian split squat (DBs at sides) — 4 × 6 each side
- Incline DB press — 3 × 8
- Chest-supported T-bar or DB row — 3 × 10
- Hip thrust (barbell, pad, moderate load) — 3 × 8
- Half-kneeling cable chop (hips square, no spinal rotation — movement is shoulders/arms) — 3 × 10 each side
- Stir-the-pot on stability ball — 3 × 6 each direction

**Weekly progression:**
- Week 5: establish working weights.
- Week 6: +2.5-5kg on main lifts, add 1 rep on accessories.
- Week 7: push to 2 RIR on top sets.
- Week 8: deload — volume cut by ~40%, intensity ~80% of week 7.

**Red flags to watch:** any radicular symptoms (leg pain, numbness, tingling), morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, or end-of-set lumbar discomfort. If any appear, regress load and check his sleep, hydration, and desk posture before progressing again.

---

## Phase 3 — Strength Expression & Robustness (Weeks 9-12)

**Goal:** Heaviest loading of the programme on safe patterns. Top sets at 1-2 RIR. Introduce a small power element if movement quality is good.

### Session A

- Safety bar squat or front squat — work up to 1 × 3 @ RPE 8, then 3 × 4 back-off
- Bench press — work up to 1 × 3 @ RPE 8, then 3 × 5
- Weighted chin-up — 4 × 5
- Pallof press iso-hold — 3 × 20 sec each side
- Hollow body hold (neutral spine, no flexion) — 3 × 20-30 sec

### Session B

- Trap bar deadlift from blocks — work up to 1 × 3 @ RPE 8, then 3 × 4
- Landmine push press — 3 × 5 each side
- Single-arm DB row, heavy — 4 × 6 each side
- Walking lunge with DBs — 3 × 8 each leg
- Heavy farmer's carry — 4 × 30m
- Side plank with top-leg abduction — 3 × 30 sec each side

### Session C

- Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated) — 4 × 5 each side, heaviest of the programme
- Incline DB press — 4 × 6
- Half-kneeling single-arm pulldown — 3 × 8 each side
- Hip thrust — work up to 1 × 5 @ RPE 8
- KB swing, light-moderate, hip-driven, neutral spine (introduce here only if he's symptom-free and hinging well) — 3 × 10
- Loaded carry of choice (suitcase or front-rack) — 3 × 40m

**Weekly progression:**
- Week 9: introduce top single, conservative load.
- Week 10: add small load to top set, +1 rep on back-offs.
- Week 11: peak week — heaviest top sets of the programme, still 1 RIR.
- Week 12: testing/deload week. Establish new 3RMs on trap bar, front squat, and bench. Lower volume by 50%.

---

## Daily Trunk & Mobility (5-10 min, pre-session or at home)

Run McGill's "Big 3" most days, and these mobility drills before each session:

- Cat-camel (unloaded, gentle ROM) — 8 reps
- 90/90 hip stretch — 30 sec each side
- World's greatest stretch — 3 each side
- Thoracic extension over a foam roller — 8 reps
- Glute bridge — 10 reps
- McGill curl-up — 3 × 5-sec holds
- Side plank — 2 × 20-30 sec each side
- Bird-dog — 2 × 6 each side

## Desk & Lifestyle

Tell him bluntly: the gym work won't fix what eight hours of slumped sitting undoes. He needs to:

- Get up and walk for 2-3 min every 30-45 minutes.
- Aim for 8,000+ steps daily.
- Sleep 7+ hours — disc tissue hydrates overnight; this matters more than people think.
- Avoid heavy lifting in the first hour after waking (discs are at peak hydration and pressure).

## Recovery

- One full rest day between sessions minimum.
- Encourage Zone 2 cardio on off days — 30-40 min walking, cycling, or swimming. Avoid running early in the programme.
- If he reports back tightness, default response is a walk, not a stretch.

## Nutrition (Light Touch)

You didn't ask for detailed macros, but as a desk worker rebuilding strength I'd suggest:

- Protein: ~1.6-2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily, spread across 3-4 meals.
- Hydration: 35 ml/kg/day minimum — disc health depends on it.
- Don't run a calorie deficit during this programme; he needs to recover. Maintenance or slight surplus is ideal.

---

## Reassessment Points

- **End of week 4:** movement quality check on hinge, squat, single-leg. Any symptoms? Progress or hold.
- **End of week 8:** strength check on trap bar, front squat, bench. Compare to baselines.
- **End of week 12:** 3RM testing, then a planned 1-week deload before any next block.

If at week 12 he's asymptomatic and moving well, a sensible next block introduces conventional deadlift from a slight elevation, or back squat with submaximal loads — but get physio sign-off before crossing either of those lines.
